mainTopic: Three teachings of רבי שמעון בן יוחי (via רבי ירמיה): adding a day to the festival (איסור חג), using מצוה objects דרך גדילתן (in the way they grow), and רשב״י's merit that protects the whole world.
overview: The amud opens with the פסוק "אסרו חג בעבותים" and reads it as a source for celebrating a festive add-on day after the חג, which is credited like bringing a קרבן. More teachings of רבי שמעון בן יוחי follow through the same chain. מצוה objects must be used דרך גדילתן, learned from "עצי שטים עומדים", and a ברייתא adds two more readings of that word. רשב״י also describes how his merit can protect the world, and says the truly elevated are very few. The גמרא challenges this from רבא (18,000) and אביי (36) and answers by describing higher and higher levels of closeness to the שכינה. Back in the משנה, the גמרא explains that the people thanked ה׳ and praised the מזבח as two separate things. It then gives two reasons for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's palm branches: the plural כפות, and רבי לוי's image of ישראל's one heart. Finally, שמואל, רבה בר בר חנה and רבין disagree about how many days the ברכה on לולב and סוכה is said. רב יוסף tells us to follow רבה בר בר חנה, and a ברייתא challenging that view begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Adding a festive day counts like bringing an offering
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "אסרו חג בעבותים" is read a new way: whoever makes an איסור לחג with eating and drinking is credited as if he built a מזבח and offered a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Bind the festival with thick branches until the horns of the altar." רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, and רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון המחוזי in the name of רבי יוחנן המכותי: Anyone who makes an 'attachment' to the festival with eating and drinking, the verse treats him as if he built an altar and brought an offering on it. As it says: "Bind the festival with thick branches until the horns of the altar."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from תהלים and gives a teaching from it. Celebrating with a festive meal right after the חג is treated like offering a קרבן on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אסרו" (bind) is read as "attach": you attach an extra day to the חג. The word "עבותים" is read as fattened animals, meaning festive eating. Since the פסוק ends with "the horns of the מזבח", that festive eating is compared to bringing a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'bind the festival'. Read here as 'attach a day to the festival'
With thick branches (the myrtle). Read here as 'with fattened animals', meaning festive food
An add-on day attached to the festival, celebrated with a meal
The verse credits him as if...
The horns (raised corners) of the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The same פסוק is used in two different ways. Right before this, it was about binding the לולב and myrtle. Here, "אסרו חג" means attaching an extra day to the חג. Do not mix up the two readings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of אסרו חג, the day after a festival, which is still observed with some extra celebration today.

phrases.english: "Bind the festival with thick branches
phrases.notes: This is תהלים קי״ח:כ״ז. It picks up the earlier talk about tying the לולב together with the myrtle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַמָּחוֹזִי

in the name of Rabbi Yochanan HaMakkoti:
Anyone who makes an attachment to the festival

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה אִיסּוּר לֶחָג בַּאֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק from the earlier לולב discussion and gives it a second meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making a festive meal as an add-on to the חג is credited like building a מזבח and offering a קרבן.

steps.title: מצוה objects must be held the way they grow
steps.stepSummary: Using the same chain of transmission, the גמרא brings another teaching: you only fulfill a מצוה with an object when it is positioned דרך גדילתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said that רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: With all the מצוות, a person only fulfills them in the way the objects grow. As it says: "Acacia wood, standing."
steps.whatsHappening: Since a teaching from רבי ירמיה in the name of רשב״י was just quoted, the גמרא brings another one from him. מצוה objects, like the לולב, must be held right-side up, the way they grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source is the beams of the משכן, described as "standing". That is read to mean they stood the way the trees grew, with the bottom down. רשב״י makes this a general rule for every מצוה, which is why the לולב must be held with its base down.

keyTerms.meaning: In the way they grow (bottom down, top up)
Acacia wood, used for the beams of the משכן

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה that a לולב (and other מצוה objects) held upside down is not valid.

phrases.english: Chizkiya said that Rabbi Yirmeya said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
All the מצוות, every one of them,
a person does not fulfill them
except in the way they grow,
as it says: "Acacia wood, standing."
phrases.notes: שמות כ״ו:ט״ו, about the beams of the משכן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Linked to step 1 only because it has the same chain of transmission. It is a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מצוה object must be used דרך גדילתן.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the 'way they grow' reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads "עומדים" the same way: the beams stood as they grew.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: "Acacia wood, standing" means that they stand the way they grew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רשב״י's reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that "עומדים" means standing upright as the tree grew. This backs up the source used in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: This was also taught in a ברייתא (a supporting source)

phrases.english: It was also taught so:
"Acacia wood, standing" —
that they stand the way they grew.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רשב״י's reading that "עומדים" means דרך גדילתן.

steps.title: Second reading: the beams hold up their plating
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers another meaning of "עומדים": the beams hold their gold covering in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "standing" means that they hold up their plating.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second, different reading of the word "עומדים".
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here "עומדים" is about function. The wooden beams support the gold covering that was nailed onto them. This is a different reading of the word, not a challenge to the first one.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "standing" —
that they hold up their plating.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same word in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "עומדים" means the beams support their gold plating.

steps.title: Third reading: the beams last forever
steps.stepSummary: A third reading: "עומדים" teaches that the משכן beams were not lost forever. They stand for all time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: "standing". In case you might say their hope is lost and their chance is gone, the verse says "acacia wood, standing", meaning they stand forever and ever.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third reading. The beams of the משכן still exist and will be used again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think that once the משכן was put away, its beams lost all purpose. "עומדים" teaches that they endure forever. This is a message of hope for the future.
steps.whatToRemember: "עצי שטים עומדים" has three readings. First, דרך גדילתן, which is the source for holding מצוה objects as they grow. Second, the beams hold up their plating. Third, the beams last forever.

phrases.english: Another explanation: "standing" —
lest you say
their hope is lost and their chance is gone,
the verse teaches: "Acacia wood, standing" —
that they stand forever and for all eternity.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: עוֹמְדִים שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר אָבַד סִיבְרָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same word.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The beams of the משכן endure forever.

steps.title: רשב״י's merit can protect the whole world
steps.stepSummary: רשב״י says his merit can free the world from judgment from his lifetime until now. With his son רבי אליעזר, it reaches back to creation. With יותם בן עוזיהו, it reaches to the end of time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חזקיה said that רבי ירמיה said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: I can free the entire world from judgment from the day I was created until now. If my son אליעזר were with me, from the day the world was created until now. If יותם בן עוזיהו were with us, from the day the world was created until its end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching with the same chain. This one is aggadic: רשב״י describes how far his merit can protect the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement builds in three levels. רשב״י alone covers the time from his birth until now. Adding his son covers all of history until now. Adding the righteous king יותם covers until the end of the world. The point is that the merit of great צדיקים can outweigh the sins of whole generations.
steps.whatToRemember: This passage brings three teachings from רבי ירמיה in the name of רשב״י: אסרו חג, דרך גדילתן, and the protective merit of צדיקים.

phrases.english: And Chizkiya said that Rabbi Yirmeya said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
I am able to free

phrases.aramaic: אֶת כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ מִן הַדִּין —
phrases.english: the entire world from judgment —
from the day I was created until now,
and if Eliezer my son were with me —
from the day the world was created until now,
and if Yotam ben Uziyahu were with us —
from the day the world was created until its end.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching with the same chain of transmission. It is a new, aggadic topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The merit of רשב״י, his son, and יותם בן עוזיהו can protect the world from judgment.

steps.title: The truly elevated are very few
steps.stepSummary: רשב״י says the truly elevated people are few, and he and his son are always among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חזקיה said in the name of רבי ירמיה, who said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: I have seen the people of the highest level, and they are few. If there are a thousand, my son and I are among them. If there are a hundred, my son and I are among them. If there are only two, they are my son and I.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same chain of transmission as before, the גמרא brings another statement of רשב״י. He says the people on the highest spiritual level are very few.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number shrinks from a thousand, to a hundred, to two, but רשב״י and his son are always included. This statement sets up the next questions: just how few are these people?

keyTerms.meaning: People of the highest spiritual level
My son and I (רשב״י and רבי אליעזר)

phrases.english: And Chizkiya said that Rabbi Yirmeya said
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
I have seen the people of the highest level, and they are few.

phrases.aramaic: אִם אֶלֶף הֵן — אֲנִי וּבְנִי מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: If they are a thousand, my son and I are among them;

phrases.aramaic: אִם מֵאָה הֵם — אֲנִי וּבְנִי מֵהֶן,
phrases.english: if they are a hundred, my son and I are among them;

phrases.aramaic: אִם שְׁנַיִם הֵן — אֲנִי וּבְנִי הֵן.
phrases.english: if they are two, my son and I are they.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רשב״י, passed down through the same chain as step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The truly elevated צדיקים are very few, and רשב״י and his son are always among them.

steps.title: Challenge: רבא counts eighteen thousand
steps.stepSummary: רבא says 18,000 צדיקים stand before ה׳, so how can רשב״י say there are so few?
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really that few? But רבא said: there is a row of eighteen thousand before הקדוש ברוך הוא, as the verse says: "Around, eighteen thousand."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רשב״י. רבא says 18,000 צדיקים stand before ה׳, which is far more than "two."
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the verse in יחזקאל as describing 18,000 righteous people surrounding ה׳. That number seems to clash with רשב״י's claim that there may be only two.

phrases.english: And are they really that few?
But didn't Rava say:
There is a row of eighteen thousand
before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
as it says: "Around, eighteen thousand"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי זוּטְרֵי כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the small number given in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רשב״י's claim that the elevated are very few
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא counts 18,000 צדיקים before ה׳, which contradicts a count of only two

steps.title: Two levels: the clear view and the less clear view
steps.stepSummary: רשב״י means those who see through a clear lens. רבא means those who do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. One statement refers to those who look through a clear lens. The other refers to those who do not look through a clear lens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two statements are talking about different levels of צדיקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a tiny group perceives the שכינה clearly, through the "bright lens," and those are the few that רשב״י means. The 18,000 of רבא are צדיקים on a lower level. So both statements are true.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the opening of an answer)
A clear, bright lens: a clear perception of the שכינה

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one refers to those who look through the clear lens,
that one refers to those who do not look through the clear lens.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּמִסְתַּכְּלִי בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements describe the same group of צדיקים
steps.terutzMaskana: רשב״י refers to the few with a clear view. רבא refers to the larger group without one.

steps.title: Challenge: אביי counts thirty-six
steps.stepSummary: Even those with the clear view number at least 36, according to אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are those who look through the clear lens really that few? But אביי said: the world never has fewer than thirty-six צדיקים who greet the שכינה every day, as the verse says: "Happy are all who wait for Him (לו)." The word לו has the numerical value of thirty-six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. Even the top group, those with the clear view, seems to be at least 36 people, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי learns from the גימטריא of לו (ל=30, ו=6) that 36 צדיקים greet the שכינה daily. That is a much higher number than רשב״י's "two," even for the highest level.

keyTerms.meaning: They greet the face of the שכינה
The world never has fewer than

phrases.english: And those who look through the clear lens,
are they really that few?
But didn't Abaye say:

phrases.aramaic: לָא פָּחֵית עָלְמָא מִתְּלָתִין וְשִׁיתָּא צַדִּיקֵי
phrases.english: The world has no fewer than thirty-six righteous people
who greet the Divine Presence every day,
as it says: "Happy are all who wait for Him (lo)";
"lo" in numerical value is thirty-six!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְמִסְתַּכְּלִי בְּאַסְפַּקְלַרְיָא הַמְּאִירָה, מִי זוּטְרֵי כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that those with the clear view are only a very few
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי says at least 36 greet the שכינה every day, which is more than two

steps.title: With permission or without permission
steps.stepSummary: The 36 enter the presence of the שכינה with permission. רשב״י's few enter without needing permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. One statement refers to those who enter with permission. The other refers to those who enter without permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to an even higher level inside the group of 36.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's 36 must ask permission before coming close to the שכינה. רשב״י's tiny group can enter at any time without asking. So even among the 36, only a very few reach that top level.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. 18,000 צדיקים do not have the clear view. 36 have the clear view but enter with permission. A tiny few, like רשב״י and his son, enter without needing permission.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one refers to those who enter with permission,
that one refers to those who enter without permission.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דְּעָיְילִי בְּבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone with the clear view is on the same level
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי's 36 enter with permission. רשב״י's few enter without permission.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: what they said when leaving
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about what the people said when they left the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time they left, what did they say? (and so on in the משנה)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its words about what the people said as they left at the end of the חג. This is a setup line for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two versions. The תנא קמא says they called out "יופי לך מזבח" (beauty to you, מזבח). רבי אליעזר says they called out "ליה ולך מזבח" (to ה׳ and to you, מזבח), which mentions ה׳ and the מזבח in one phrase. The גמרא is about to question that second wording.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: At the time of their leaving
what would they say, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁעַת פְּטִירָתָן מָה הֵן אוֹמְרִים וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadah and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people praised the מזבח and ה׳ as they left.

steps.title: Challenge: joining ה׳ with something else
steps.stepSummary: Praising ה׳ and the מזבח together seems to join ה׳'s name with another thing, which is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are joining the name of Heaven with something else! And a ברייתא teaches: anyone who joins the name of Heaven with something else is uprooted from the world, as the verse says: "except to ה׳ alone."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. Putting ה׳ and the מזבח together in one praise looks like a serious sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא forbids joining ה׳'s name with any other thing, based on "בלתי לה׳ לבדו." The praise in the משנה seems to do exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of Heaven together with something else

phrases.english: But they are joining
the name of Heaven and something else,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא: כׇּל הַמְשַׁתֵּף שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְדָבָר אַחֵר
phrases.english: and it was taught: Anyone who joins the name of Heaven and something else
is uprooted from the world,
as it says: "except to the Lord alone"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא קָא מִשְׁתַּתַּף שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם וְדָבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the praise quoted in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The praise of ה׳ and the מזבח said together
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids joining ה׳'s name with anything else

steps.title: Two separate praises
steps.stepSummary: They thanked ה׳ and praised the מזבח as two separate things.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they meant: to ה׳ we give thanks, and you (the מזבח) we praise. To ה׳ we give thanks, and you we acclaim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words so that ה׳ and the מזבח are clearly kept apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thanks and acknowledgment go to ה׳ alone. The מזבח gets a different, separate kind of praise. Because the two are not combined into one praise, there is no forbidden joining.

phrases.english: This is what they are saying:

phrases.aramaic: לְיָהּ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים, וְלָךְ אָנוּ מְשַׁבְּחִין.
phrases.english: To God we give thanks, and you we praise.

phrases.aramaic: לְיָהּ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים, וְלָךְ אָנוּ מְקַלְּסִין.
phrases.english: To God we give thanks, and you we acclaim.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: לְיָהּ אֲנַחְנוּ מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ה׳ and the מזבח were praised together as one
steps.terutzMaskana: Thanks went to ה׳ alone. Separate praise went to the מזבח.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: as on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, which includes רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view on palm branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was done on a weekday (so it was done on שבת...).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. This sets up a discussion of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, whose view about palm branches appears in that part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that part of the משנה, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says palm branches (חריות של דקל) were brought and beaten on the ground beside the מזבח. The quote opens the search for the source of his view.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was done on a weekday

phrases.english: As its performance on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַעֲשֵׂהוּ בַּחוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The service was done on שבת the same way as on a weekday.

steps.title: What is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's source?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא asks for the reason behind bringing palm branches for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is the reason of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא asks what verse רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה bases his view on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question asks for the source of the palm-branch practice at the מזבח. רב הונא answers it himself in the next step.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה,
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the view in the משנה quoted in step 15
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse behind bringing palm branches for the מזבח

steps.title: כפות means two
steps.stepSummary: The plural word כפות means two branches: one for the לולב and one for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written "כפות" (branches, plural), which means two: one for the לולב and one for the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his own question with the plural word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The minimum plural is two. One branch is used for the לולב. The second one must be for something else, so it goes to the מזבח.

phrases.english: As it is written "kappot" (branches), meaning two:
one for the lulav and one for the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״כַּפּוֹת״, שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural כפות means two: one branch for the לולב and one for the מזבח

steps.title: The רבנן read it as one branch
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן say the word is spelled without a ו, so it means only one branch.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: it is written "כפת" (without a ו), which means one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן disagree: they follow how the word is written, not how it is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is read "כפות" but written without a ו, so it can be read as the singular "כפת." Based on the spelling, only one branch is needed, and that one is for the לולב. So there is no source for a separate branch for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: One branch (singular, based on the spelling)

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides read the same word in the פסוק. רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה follows the way it is read (כפות, plural). The רבנן follow the way it is written (כפת, without a ו, singular).

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
"kappat" (singular) is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: ״כַּפַּת״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The spelling כפת means one branch, so no extra branch for the מזבח comes from this פסוק.

steps.title: רבי לוי: ישראל has one heart, like the date palm
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי gives a different reason for the palm-branch custom. A date palm has one heart, and so does ישראל toward their Father in Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי says: it is because of the date palm. Just as a date palm has only one heart, so too ישראל has only one heart, directed to their Father in Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives his own answer to רב הונא's question about why palm branches were brought for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer took the reason from the plural word כפות in the פסוק. רבי לוי does not use the פסוק at all. He says the custom praises ישראל: a palm grows one straight trunk with no side branches, and ישראל is just as single-hearted in serving ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: One heart: a single, undivided loyalty
Their Father in Heaven, meaning ה׳

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi says: it is like a date palm:
phrases.notes: A reason based on symbolism, not on a פסוק.

phrases.english: Just as this date palm
has only one heart,
phrases.notes: The trunk grows straight up, with branches only at the top.

phrases.english: so too, the Jewish people have only
one heart
toward their Father in Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי לֵוִי אוֹמֵר, כְּתָמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to רב הונא's question, replacing the reading of the word כפות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The palm-branch custom praises ישראל, who have one heart toward ה׳, just as a palm has one heart.

steps.title: שמואל: ברכה on לולב seven days, on סוכה one day
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the ברכה on לולב is said all seven days, but the ברכה on סוכה is said only on one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: לולב gets a ברכה seven days, and סוכה gets a ברכה one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: on how many days do we say a ברכה on לולב and on סוכה? שמואל gives the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because the תורה clearly commands sitting in the סוכה for all seven days. Even so, שמואל says the סוכה ברכה is said only once, so the גמרא will need to explain his reason.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken on סוכות, here meaning the ברכה over it
The festival booth, here meaning the ברכה over sitting in it
Seven, meaning all seven days of the festival

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is NOT saying the מצוה of סוכה lasts only one day. Everyone agrees you sit in the סוכה all seven days. The argument is only about how many days you say the ברכה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
For lulav, the blessing is said seven days,
and for sukkah, the blessing is said one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, about ברכות on the festival מצוות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on לולב is said all seven days. The ברכה on סוכה is said only on one day.

steps.title: Why שמואל ruled this way: nights split the days
steps.stepSummary: The לולב מצוה stops each night, so each day is a new מצוה. The סוכה מצוה continues through the nights, so all seven days count as one long day.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? With לולב, the nights separate the days, so each day is its own separate מצוה. With סוכה, the nights do not separate the days, so all seven days are like one long day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for שמואל's reason and then explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You do not take a לולב at night, so the מצוה stops and starts again each morning. A new start means a new ברכה. You do sit in the סוכה at night, so the מצוה never stops. The first ברכה covers the whole festival.

keyTerms.meaning: A מצוה standing on its own

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Lulav, where the nights are separated from the days,
phrases.notes: There is no לולב מצוה at night.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יוֹמָא מִצְוָה בְּאַפֵּיהּ נַפְשֵׁיהּ הוּא.
phrases.english: each day is a מצוה in and of itself.
Sukkah, where the nights are not separated from the days,
phrases.notes: The סוכה מצוה applies at night as well.

phrases.english: all seven days
are like one long day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מצוה that stops each night needs a new ברכה each day. A מצוה that continues day and night needs only one ברכה.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: סוכה seven days, לולב one day
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says the exact opposite of שמואל: the סוכה ברכה is said seven days and the לולב ברכה only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: סוכה gets a ברכה seven days, and לולב gets a ברכה one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion that flips שמואל's ruling completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל looked at whether the מצוה stops at night. This opinion will look at something else: whether each מצוה comes from the תורה or from the רבנן.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
For sukkah, the blessing is said seven days,
and for lulav, the blessing is said one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An opposing opinion to שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on סוכה is said all seven days. The ברכה on לולב is said only on one day.

steps.title: Why: סוכה is from the תורה, לולב is דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: סוכה is a תורה מצוה all seven days, so it gets a ברכה every day. לולב after the first day is only דרבנן, so one day of ברכה is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? סוכה is from the תורה all seven days, so it gets a ברכה seven days. לולב is from the רבנן, so one day is enough for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason for רבה בר בר חנה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside the מקדש, the תורה requires לולב only on the first day. The other days were added by the רבנן. So this view gives a full daily ברכה only to the מצוה that is from the תורה every day, which is סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the רבנן, a rabbinic enactment

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Sukkah, which is from the Torah, gets seven days,
lulav, which is rabbinic
phrases.notes: This refers to the days after the first day.

phrases.english: one day is enough for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? סוּכָּה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רבה בר בר חנה's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The number of days of ברכה depends on whether the מצוה is from the תורה (seven days) or דרבנן (one day).

steps.title: רבין's report: both get a ברכה all seven days
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings a different version of רבי יוחנן's teaching: both סוכה and לולב get a ברכה all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: both this one and that one get a ברכה seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion arrives: a different report of what רבי יוחנן said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two conflicting reports of רבי יוחנן's view. Both reports agree that סוכה gets a ברכה all seven days. They disagree only about לולב: one day or seven.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Both this one and that one

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Both this and that get the blessing seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A conflicting report of רבי יוחנן's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברכה on both סוכה and לולב is said all seven days.

steps.title: רב יוסף: follow רבה בר בר חנה, who is confirmed on סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says to hold on to רבה בר בר חנה's teaching, because on the question of סוכה all the אמוראים agree with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Hold on to the teaching of רבה בר בר חנה, because all the אמוראים agree with him about סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף tells us to rely on רבה בר בר חנה's report of רבי יוחנן's view. His reason is that on סוכה, all the other reporters agree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two conflicting reports of רבי יוחנן's view. רבין agrees with רבה בר בר חנה that סוכה gets a ברכה all seven days, so רבה בר בר חנה's version is confirmed on that point. רב יוסף therefore treats his whole report as the reliable one, including that the לולב ברכה is said only one day.

keyTerms.meaning: Hold it in your hand: rely on this
The אמוראים, here the scholars who reported רבי יוחנן's teachings

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: שמואל says לולב seven days and סוכה one. רבה בר בר חנה says סוכה seven and לולב one. רבין says both seven. רב יוסף says to hold on to רבה בר בר חנה's report, since everyone agrees with him on סוכה. A ברייתא now challenges that position.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practice of saying the לישב בסוכה ברכה every day of סוכות.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: נְקוֹט דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה בִּידָךְ,
phrases.english: Take the statement of Rabba bar bar Ḥana in your hand,
since all the amora'im
hold in accordance with him regarding sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נְקוֹט דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה בִּידָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides among the three opinions, regarding סוכה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Follow רבה בר בר חנה's report: the ברכה on סוכה is said all seven days and the ברכה on לולב one day. His version is trusted because all the אמוראים agree with him on סוכה.

steps.title: The גמרא introduces an objection from a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The word מֵיתִיבִי signals that a ברייתא is about to be quoted to challenge the view the גמרא just accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is announcing that it is about to quote a ברייתא that seems to conflict with what was just said. The ברייתא itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מֵיתִיבִי always means an objection is coming from a תנאי source, such as a משנה or ברייתא. An אמורא is expected to agree with such sources. Right after רב יוסף told us to follow רבה בר בר חנה, the גמרא is checking that ruling against an earlier teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה. It carries authority over אמוראים.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up מֵיתִיבִי with אִיתְּמַר or תָּא שְׁמַע. מֵיתִיבִי means a challenge is coming, not just a new statement and not necessarily a proof. Also, this line holds no content yet. Wait for the ברייתא in the next lines before deciding what is being challenged.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge what was just said. The ברייתא itself comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Right after רב יוסף's ruling to follow רבה בר בר חנה in step 25, the גמרא opens a challenge from a ברייתא against the accepted position.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברכה rules for סוכה and לולב that were just accepted in steps 22-25, especially רבה בר בר חנה's view in the name of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא, which carries תנאי authority, is about to be quoted. Its wording seems to conflict with the accepted ruling. The details follow on the next amud.
